ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and subsequent amendments; Executive Regulations under Prime Ministerial Decree No. 811/2003 as amended; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT sectoral regulations; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and GAFI implementing decisions requiring disclosure of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership information to the Egyptian Commercial Registry and the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each shareholder, director, and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent passport authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the country of issue; the Hague Apostille is not accepted because Egypt is not a Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin, followed by legalization at the competent Egyptian Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and/or the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or other competent corporate registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the board/shareholder resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and the appointment of its first directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of incorporation of the corporate shareholder or other competent legal authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the jurisdiction of issuance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and Ultimate Beneficial Owners against the OFAC SDN List, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT watchlist, and the domestic Egyptian PEP and terrorist-financing designations published by the EMLCU. Enhanced due diligence is required for any Politically Exposed Person or sanctions-nexus hit; results must be refreshed within 30 days prior to notarization and submission to GAFI.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Commercial Registry Name Reservation Portal, available through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) at https://www.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Arabic as the statutory legal identity. A Latin-alphabet transliteration may be registered as a secondary trading name, but the Arabic version governs. The name must not conflict with any existing registered name or trademark, must not be misleading, and must not contain any expression suggesting a governmental, military, religious, or political affiliation without explicit ministerial authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI rejects the proposed name, the applicant or its licensed legal representative may file a written Tazallum (grievance) before the GAFI Commercial Registration Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice. The grievance must state the factual and legal grounds and attach the original justification. GAFI is expected to issue a decision within 15 working days. If the grievance is denied, the applicant may escalate to the Minister of Investment's administrative review office within another 30 days, after which judicial review before the Administrative Court of the State Council is available under the Egyptian Administrative Judiciary Law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office is not accepted as the statutory registered address for an Egyptian LLC. The company must maintain a physical office, serviced office, or business center address within Egypt for service of process and tax registration. Remote delivery of 3D art production services is commercially permissible, but the registered address must be an accessible physical location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified as approximately 15% in the first full operating year and 10% in subsequent years, reflecting the low-risk AML classification of ISIC 7490 creative services, balanced against routine tax authority verification visits and occasional GAFI commercial registry spot checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, including Articles 4, 117–129 governing limited liability companies, and its Executive Regulations issued by Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended. Companies Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations apply if the company elects to incorporate under the Investment Law regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Establishment Department; the competent Commercial Registry office records the company following establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Liability Company Contract of Incorporation (Memorandum of Association) and prescribed GAFI establishment application, followed by entry in the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum capital is prescribed for an Egyptian LLC. The partners determine capital in the incorporation contract; capital contributions must be paid as required by the applicable company regime and GAFI procedures. The capital is not subject to the joint-stock-company bank deposit certificate procedure. Confirm any current GAFI payment evidence requirements before filing. The amount above is not a representation that government filing charges are zero; charges are assessed in Egyptian pounds and vary by filing and service.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company be established as an Egyptian limited liability company under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, on the terms of its approved Contract of Incorporation. The partners’ subscriptions and capital contributions are accepted as stated in that contract, and the authorized representative is directed to complete any required payment formalities. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be the address stated in the incorporation documents, subject to lawful occupancy and registration. [Name] is appointed manager, with authority and signing powers as specified in the contract, and [Name] is appointed as the Company’s authorized representative for GAFI, Commercial Registry, tax, and other establishment filings. Any prior establishment acts consistent with these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm company name, partners, managers, and business purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center (ISC), Companies Establishment Department, or GAFI's official electronic establishment service where available
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select an available company name and ensure the proposed objects accurately cover digital game-art production, 3D modeling, sculpting, rigging, and related outsourcing services. Identify partners, quota allocations, capital, manager(s), signing authority, and the registered-office address. A foreign corporate partner should prepare legalized and Arabic-translated corporate authority and existence documents. Confirm whether any regulated activity is inadvertently included in the objects.
required_dossiers: Corporate partner constitutional documents and board or member authorization, if applicable
Registered-office address evidence or lease documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name or object is rejected, submit an alternative name or narrower description consistent with the actual services. Correct partner or manager details and provide additional legalization, translation, or authority evidence requested by GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute and submit the LLC incorporation contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center (ISC), Companies Establishment Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the prescribed LLC establishment application and contract using GAFI's current forms. Arrange execution, authentication, or notarization in the manner directed by GAFI for the signatories and documents concerned; do not assume foreign signatures are effective without the required consular legalization and Arabic translation. Submit the contract, partner and manager particulars, office evidence, and applicable fee payments through the prescribed service channel.
required_dossiers: Powers of attorney or corporate authorizations, where applicable
Legalized and Arabic-translated foreign documents, where applicable
Payment receipts for assessed government charges
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to GAFI's written query within its stated deadline, amend the application or contract, and resubmit supporting documents. Where the query concerns signature or foreign-document formalities, obtain the specified notarization, legalization, and certified Arabic translation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain establishment documents and Commercial Register entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Establishment Department and the competent Commercial Registry office of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI approval, collect the establishment documents and complete the required Commercial Registry registration steps through the channel directed by GAFI. Verify that the registered name, legal form, address, managers, capital, and business objects match the approved contract. Retain certified copies and electronic records.
required_dossiers: GAFI establishment certificate or equivalent issued establishment documents
Commercial Registry application and assessed-fee receipts
Manager identity documents and powers of attorney, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of any discrepancy before relying on the registry extract. For a rejected or incomplete entry, cure the stated deficiency with GAFI or the competent Commercial Registry office and obtain an updated extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax and employer registrations before commencing operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and the competent offices of the National Authority for Social Insurance, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company tax registration and tax identification details using the establishment and Commercial Register documents. Register as an employer and enroll covered employees with the social insurance authorities before employing staff. Assess VAT registration and e-invoicing obligations against current statutory thresholds, transaction type, and ETA rules; do not treat incorporation as automatic completion of these registrations.
required_dossiers: Manager or authorized representative identification and authority
Employee and payroll information, when applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve ETA or social-insurance objections by correcting entity, address, activity, or representative data and supplying requested evidence. Obtain written confirmation of applicable VAT and e-invoicing status before issuing invoices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish ongoing LLC governance and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company managers and partners; GAFI and Commercial Registry for any filing required by a subsequent change
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the incorporation contract, partner and quota records, manager appointments, resolutions, accounting records, tax records, and supporting transaction documents at the registered office or another lawful location. Observe the contract's approval and signing rules. File and register changes to the registered office, managers, capital, partners, or objects where required before treating them as effective against third parties.
required_dossiers: Approved Contract of Incorporation and amendments
Accounting, tax, payroll, and supporting business records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficient records or approvals promptly and make any overdue GAFI or Commercial Registry filings. Obtain local counsel review before implementing a change affecting ownership, management authority, or registered particulars.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority is ordinarily required for a service-only AAA game-art outsourcing studio. The General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) handles company establishment; the competent local authority handles premises-specific requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required for digital 3D art production and outsourcing. A local premises or business operating approval may apply depending on the location, building use, and activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), under the Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinarily exempt from a project EIA for an office-based digital creative-services operation with no material emissions, industrial process, or regulated discharge. Confirm project screening with the competent authority if the site or activities change.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No activity-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-waste threshold is ordinarily triggered by office-based computer and digital art services. Comply with applicable general environmental, municipal wastewater, hazardous-waste, and e-waste requirements; obtain approvals before introducing equipment or processes that create regulated emissions or discharges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain any fire-safety or occupancy approval required for the selected premises from the competent local authority and Civil Protection authorities. The building owner or tenant should verify lawful office use, fire precautions, emergency access, and any required inspections. There is no ordinary industrial structural-load inspection or manufacturing workplace clearance for a standard office studio; workplace and social-insurance obligations apply when employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; unified digital compliance portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg, with e-filing at https://www.incometax.gov.eg and e-invoicing/e-receipt clearance at https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-invested LLC must (1) incorporate under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 via GAFI or under Companies Law No. 4 of 2018; (2) obtain commercial registration from the Commercial Registry; (3) file GAFI single-window 'golden license' data; (4) submit the ETA unified tax registration form (with notarized memorandum of association, commercial register extract, board resolution appointing the legal representative, power of attorney for the tax agent, and proof of office address); (5) receive the TIN, VAT account and electronic Tax Card (issued in approximately 10 business days). The TIN activates e-filing and e-invoicing accounts before the first taxable supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists; classification is statutory. Only relevant corporate election is fiscal-unity consolidated filing for an Egyptian parent owning at least 95% of Egyptian subsidiaries (ETA pre-approval, minimum five-year commitment, and application within three months of the relevant tax period end). Depreciation and loss-carryforward options are formulaic; treaty relief requires the ETA residence/TIN certificate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration when annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000; voluntary registration for turnover between EGP 100,000 and EGP 500,000 (VAT Law No. 67 of 2016, Art. 15). De facto unconditional for an LLC holding commercial registration because an active ETA tax file and VAT account are prerequisites for lawful invoicing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory national e-invoicing regime (phased from 15 Feb 2021, universal for all taxable persons from 15 Oct 2022): every B2B invoice must be transmitted in real time to the ETA e-invoicing platform in XML/JSON via REST/SOAP APIs; the ETA validates, assigns a UUID and single-use hash, returns an accepted cleared version, and each printed copy must carry a QR code. E-receipts (B2C) are likewise cleared (from Jan 2022). Paper or unsynced invoices are denied input VAT deduction and are deemed non-issued; digital stamping links customs import entries to the invoice registry.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 23 of VAT Law 67/2016 zero-rates exported goods and services supplied by a registered taxpayer where (i) the recipient is a non-resident outside Egypt; (ii) the service is legally and economically consumed/benefited outside Egypt; (iii) the supply is evidenced by export contracts, proof of delivery, and ETA-cleared zero-rated e-invoices; and (iv) consideration is received in foreign currency. 3D game art, sculpting and rigging services performed in Egypt but delivered to overseas game studios qualify as offshore services if no economic benefit manifests inside Egypt, supported by the service agreement, milestone acceptance, IP assignment and FX remittance records. Output VAT at 14% applies to any local portion or misuse of the exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: ETA-cleared zero-rated export e-invoice (QR-coded, accepted by the platform)
Customs export declaration (only for physical media/source-file shipments; for pure digital services substitute a digital delivery log with SHA-256 hashes and FTP/cloud transfer reports)
Signed international service contract evidencing the offshore recipient and place of beneficial use
Proof of acceptance and delivery (milestone checklist, email acceptance, rig/asset handover log)
Foreign-currency inward remittance certificate from a licensed Egyptian bank
Valid tax card and VAT registration certificate (with updated activity code)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA export-audit desk reviews XML e-invoice records, customs declarations, IP/delivery logs, bank statements and FX certificates. Non-receipt of export proceeds within 180 days triggers retroactive assessment of 14% VAT on the grossed-up service value plus delay interest and double-tax penalty; fraudulent zero-rating claims additionally attract administrative fines up to EGP 100,000, imprisonment, and a criminal fine up to five times the VAT evaded (Law 67/2016 Arts. 66-68), re-opening of prior tax periods up to six years (Income Tax Law 91/2005), and deactivation of the e-invoicing account.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) acting as the sole monetary and foreign exchange authority under Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE Exchange Control Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-float regime. Current account transactions, including trade-related payments and service fees, are generally freely convertible through official banks subject to standard documentation and anti-money laundering checks. Capital account transactions, including inbound capital injections and outbound profit remittances, are permitted but require express licensing, declaration via the CBE's electronic platform, and compliant routing through a licensed domestic bank. Dividends and branch profits may be remitted after audited financial statements and proof of tax clearance. Foreign ownership of an LLC is permitted, but capital repatriation hinges on registration of the investment with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and obtaining a certificate of compliance with the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Non-trade capital flows remain subject to de facto administrative review, which can create timing friction; however, for permitted activities such as service exports under ISIC 7490, current account settlement is reliable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received into an Egyptian banking account within 90 days of the date of shipment or customs clearance. Upon crediting, the exporter is required to surrender a designated percentage of the proceeds, currently 50%, to a licensed bank for conversion into Egyptian pounds at the prevailing market rate. The remaining 50% may be held in a foreign currency account or sold at the exporter's discretion. To trigger the receipt window, the bank must be provided with a valid customs declaration, an export contract, and the pro-forma invoice; exceptions require prior CBE approval. For service and game-art outsourcing contracts, the underlying invoice and a signed service agreement are the core evidentiary documents for the 90-day collection timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EGP and USD current account for trade settlements and service receipts)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Foreign Currency Account
Operational Account with sub-accounts for payroll and foreign currency disbursements
Operational Account (EGP) and USD Clearing Account for outbound supplier payments
Trade Finance and Settlement Account supporting documentary collections and LCs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Revolut Business, Airwallex, or Payoneer cannot provide a primary operational account for the Egyptian LLC without obtaining a CBE license or registering as a payment service aggregator with the CBE's FinTech and Innovation Unit. The CBE Law No. 194 of 2020 and the payments regulatory framework require any entity handling client funds in Egypt to be licensed as a bank, specialized payment service operator, or a third-party processor supervised by the CBE. Practical utility is limited to incoming international receipts via PayPal or similar RIFF-facilitated channels, but these cannot substitute for the mandatory local bank account used for FX surrender and tax remittance procedures. The safest treatment is to treat offshore EMIs as remote collection venues only after the underlying export service invoice has been raised and the proceeds are subsequently repatriated to a local account within the 90-day window.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the initial onboarding of an Egyptian LLC, especially for foreign-owned directors. CBE's revised AML/CFT resolutions and bank know-your-customer manuals require at least one natural-person director, general manager, or an authorized representative with a valid power of attorney to appear in person at the bank branch for an interview and biometric/photo verification. Remote opening is not permitted for new corporate clients; the CBE does not recognize full digital onboarding for non-resident directors. After onboarding, subsequent account additions can be processed through authorized signatory updates, but the first account opening remains physical. For a foreign parent seated outside Egypt, the practical route is to appoint a local resident manager as co-signatory, or to have the foreign director visit Egypt with a notarized board resolution and apostilled passport copy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity in a 100% externally owned LLC whose ultimate shareholders are private individuals resident outside Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified organizational chart from incorporation, deed of incorporation and memorandum of association, notarized and apostilled certificate of ultimate beneficial owners, passports of all individuals above 10% holding, board resolution approving account opening, business references from two tier-1 banks or legal counsel, and audited financial statements of the parent if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction geography anomaly: expected inbound payment origin jurisdictions (e.g., US, EU, Singapore) with no bilateral AML equivalency to Egypt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service agreements, purchase orders from the game publisher/client, invoicing trail, internal email correspondence demonstrating project delivery, third-party IP and licensing statements, and a consolidated transaction forecast explaining the high-volume digital service export pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid high-frequency receivable concentration: 3D art outsourcing model generates many small-to-mid-size SWIFT credits from unrelated foreign entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardized invoice register, use of a designated purpose code on each incoming transfer, signed delivery notes with agreed escrow milestones, a historical income statement showing a recurring revenue pattern, and an internal Treasury and Compliance manual describing the business's export nature. Ready access to bank auditor documentation explaining that each wire corresponds to completed digital asset deliveries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential mismatch between stated business activity (computer graphics services) and software/game IP token flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed narrative of services rendered (3D sculpting, rigging, asset integration) with sample timesheets, contractual clauses ensuring no IP transfer, project management workflow screenshots, and declarations from the client that the deliverables are work-for-hire assets and not a cryptocurrency or speculative instrument.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP exposure associated with intermediaries or local hosting partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions screening forms for each counterparty, consolidated list of SDN and OFAC checks, sworn undertakings on non-involvement of sanctioned jurisdictions, and legal opinions confirming that the Egyptian entity and all named shareholders are not PEPs exposed to an elevated corruption risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment or initial capital funding into the Egyptian LLC must be routed through a licensed Egyptian bank using the unified investment transaction purpose code. For equity capital injections, the transfer should carry Purpose Code 'C.F.' (capital formation) or the designated code set by the CBE for inward direct investment, typically '01' for issuance of shares or '03' for shareholder loans. The bank will require the GAFI-issued Investment Certificate, the notarized and legalized incorporation documents, a board resolution approving the capital increase, and an undertaking that the funds will be deposited in the capital account before conversion or restructure. The receiving bank will credit the funds to the LLC's foreign-currency capital account and, if the operating currency is EGP, execute a mandatory conversion into Egyptian pounds at the prevailing interbank rate. Non-resident shareholders must ensure the wire is denominated in USD, EUR, or GBP and includes the Company CR number in the beneficiary field; funds sent to personal accounts or unrelated third-party payees will be rejected.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound routing for trade and supplier settlements must be performed through the corporate account using the SWIFT global payment ecosystem. For low-value non-documentary service transactions (e.g., paying freelance riggers in Pakistan or Ukraine), the standard rail is a SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) with the appropriate remittance field (72 or /INT/) indicating invoice settlement and with tax reference numbers. For high-value physical or IP transfer-backed production milestones, the intended rail is either an MT103 issued unilaterally or a commercial documentary letter of credit (LC) opened by the Egyptian bank for the benefit of the overseas seller. For the 3D art outsourcing company, the primary outbound use is dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders and payments to subcontracted artists; both require documentary proof of the underlying contract, relevant withholding tax certificates, and annual corporate tax filings. Egyptian banks offer a compliant outbound wire service via CBE's centralized settlement system, but banks will require Submission of the 'MT103 Cover' instruction, the supporting invoice, and the tax declaration where applicable. For dividends, an 'outward profit remittance' application must be supported by the audited balance sheet, tax clearance, and a board resolution approving the distribution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: In-market non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/EGP are permissible only through licensed Egyptian commercial banks and on the CBE's electronic trading platform; however, the CBE discourages unrestricted speculative use and limits maturity to 365 days for corporates with an underlying real transaction exposure

Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts (outright forwards) between the Egyptian LLC and its corporate bank, supported by a confirmed export or import purchase order, are permissible and can be executed in USD, EUR, or GBP against EGP
Cross-currency swaps between the LLC's non-EGP working capital and EGP operating cash flows, subject to CBE reporting and an actual underlying commercial debt or receivable
Foreign-currency options (collar, call, or put structures) with a duly licensed Egyptian bank, permissible when the notional is aligned with the projected export invoices

Interest rate and currency basis swaps involving the Egyptian pound are de facto not permissible without express CBE authorization; for the 3D art outsourcing entity with low balance-sheet leverage, plain vanilla forwards plus a policy of netting foreign currency cash flows is the lowest-risk hedging application

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19) with attached Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Electronic Filing Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year end (on or before April 30 for calendar-year LLC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EGP 5,000 per month or part thereof (capped at EGP 50,000); delay interest on unpaid tax at 2% per month; unresolved non-filing triggers administrative seizure, tax-evasion audit, and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Affirmation and Register of Members Update (share-transfer recording)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the audited financial statements (within 4 months of fiscal year end); any LLC quota transfer within 30 days of execution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EGP 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment under AML Law No. 80/2002 and Ministerial Decree 60/2019; unrecorded transfers are unenforceable against third parties and undistributable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Activity License (Mahall/Temporary License) Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before December 31 of each calendar year (annual validity).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal surcharge of 25% of the annual fee plus daily delay fines (approx. EGP 100/day); continued operation without a valid license risks premises closure and suspension of activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GAFI Annual Commercial Registration File Fee and Compliance Affidavit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of commercial registration (within 30 days after each incorporation anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of investment-law benefits and incentives; fines up to EGP 200,000 under Investment Law No. 72/2017 for repeated non-compliance; persistent default may lead to administrative strike-off of the commercial registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory independent audit is compulsory for every Egyptian LLC regardless of size; audited annual financial statements must be attached to the CIT return and approved by the shareholders' meeting (Companies Law No. 159/1981; Investment Law No. 72/2017). No small-company exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), converged with IFRS, per Ministerial Decree No. 110/2015; EAS 1 for presentation of financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under AML Law No. 80/2002 and Decree No. 60/2019, the LLC must maintain a fully populated UBO register at its registered office; every transfer of LLC quotas or indirect change in beneficial ownership must be entered and filed with the Commercial Registry within 30 days; the annual audit must verify UBO accuracy in the management letter and shareholder transfers require notarized transfer minutes to be legally effective.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Statutory and Accounting Books (Journal and Ledger)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No automatic statutory tax holiday for ordinary LLCs. Qualifying investment projects under Investment Law No. 72/2017 may obtain a CIT reduction of up to 50% for up to 5 years, and Free Zone projects may be exempt from CIT on capital and trading profits subject to an annual fee. A game art outsourcing studio using normal onshore LLC status remains subject to the 22.5% standard CIT rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 8 under Income Tax Law No. 91/2005, submitted electronically through the Egypt Tax Authority e-portal (www.etax.gov.eg).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; large taxpayers may be required to make quarterly advance CIT payments against the same Form No. 8 cycle.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the close of the accounting fiscal year. A 31 December year-end therefore requires filing and final payment by 30 April; a 30 June year-end requires filing by 31 October.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer legal identity, Commercial Registration number, Tax Card number and head office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company with an Egyptian branch must enter the branch registration number and the foreign parent's jurisdiction; no separate Egyptian legal entity number is used for the branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable period dates and fiscal year-end as declared in financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian branch's audited statutory accounting period; do not substitute the foreign parent's fiscal year unless identical.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity and ISIC code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must describe the precise Egyptian PE activity, e.g. '3D game art production services via Egyptian branch', and use ISIC 7490 when applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, export revenue, and Egyptian-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose only Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the PE; offshore turnkey deliveries with no PE activity remain outside the Egyptian return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: staff salaries, software licenses, rendering hardware depreciation, outsourcing subcontract costs, rent, utilities, and communications.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches may deduct actual head-office cost allocations only if supported by transfer pricing documentation and a cost-sharing memorandum; intercompany markups are not automatically deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions and transfer pricing schedules, including cross-border payments to the foreign parent or sister studios.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every non-resident transaction exceeding the Egyptian TP threshold must be disclosed with a benchmark study and an arm's length pricing policy.
Only losses realized through the Egyptian PE may be carried forward; foreign-parent losses are never admitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income and CIT at 22.5%, with reconciliation from accounting profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches apply the same 22.5% rate on Egyptian-source PE profit; branch repatriation tax is computed separately.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine under Tax Procedures Law No. 27/2021, typically ranging from EGP 500 to EGP 50,000, plus monthly late-payment interest on the unpaid tax at the Central Bank discount rate and an additional delinquency surcharge in serious cases. Persistent non-filing can result in an estimated assessment under Law No. 91/2005, denial of expenses, and referral to tax evasion enforcement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to its shareholder, whether resident or non-resident, unless reduced or exempted under an applicable double tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence, complete the Egyptian DTA relief application through the e-portal, and provide a beneficial ownership declaration to the paying LLC before distribution. The Egyptian withholding agent applies the reduced treaty rate after the Egypt Tax Authority approves the relief; if excess WHT is withheld, a refund claim must be filed within the statutory refund window with supporting TRC and transaction evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT is 20% on royalties and 20% on interest paid to non-residents. Egyptian DTAs typically provide rates of 5% to 15% for royalties and 0% to 15% for interest, subject to TRC, beneficial ownership, and the absence of a permanent establishment in Egypt.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million in aggregate related-party transactions triggers mandatory Local File preparation; Master File becomes obligatory where the consolidated group turnover exceeds EGP 200 million. The documentation must be submitted within 30 days of the Egypt Tax Authority's request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has not enacted UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the Egyptian Tax Authority applies substance-over-form, controlled-foreign-company and beneficial-ownership rules under Law No. 91/2005 and the Tax Procedures Law. A game 3D art outsourcing LLC must maintain actual Egyptian management, payroll, hardware, software, contracts, and delivery capacity; a letterbox company with no real staff is exposed to PE, anti-abuse, and DTA denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting foreign client invoices from revenue, fabricating subcontractor costs, or under-reporting PayPal and wire-transfer receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to EGP 500,000, plus payment of evaded tax, late-interest, and a civil penalty calculated on the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt, subjected to travel bans and asset seizure, and criminally prosecuted for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging royalties, management fees, or outsourcing margins to a foreign parent that do not comply with the arm's length standard and lack a benchmark study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profit, disallowance of the excessive intercompany deduction, interest on underpaid CIT, and penalties of up to 100% of the tax under-assessment under Egyptian TP rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for the adjusted tax if they executed the intercompany agreements and intentionally caused the mispricing; professional negligence claims are available against external TP advisors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an Egyptian LLC solely to channel service fees to a foreign parent without Egyptian office, staff, servers, or managerial decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization of revenue, denial of treaty benefits, deemed permanent establishment status for the foreign parent, retroactive CIT, WHT and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors may be personally exposed for fraudulent asset protection and are also subject to immigration travel bans during tax enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repatriating profits disguised as loans, loans disguised as royalty-free advances, or failing to apply 10% dividend WHT / 20% royalty WHT before transferring funds abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax is recovered from the Egyptian LLC together with late-payment interest, fines of up to 100% of the withheld amount, and criminal prosecution for breach of Tax Procedures Law No. 27/2021.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors responsible for the remittance are jointly liable for the un-withheld tax and may face personal criminal sanctions, including imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unregistered mule accounts, shell payment intermediaries, or untraceable cryptocurrency to receive client funds, or accepting third-party funds with no underlying contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Asset freezing, fines under the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law and Central Bank regulations, confiscation of proceeds, and referral to the Public Prosecutor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and compliance officers face personal criminal liability for failing to identify beneficial owners and report suspicious wire or PayPal transactions, including imprisonment and personal fines.
